title: fisc published column
description: Everything the chart needs for one published column of the city's budget. KEYED BY COLUMN AND NOT BY YEAR: a column is (fiscal_year, basis), and one basis per year is a property of today's corpus rather than a guarantee -- the day it prints FY2026 revised beside FY2026 adopted, a per-year name collides.

nodes.description: ONE TABLE SHARED BY EVERY SCHEDULE, CARRYING ONLY WHAT THEY AGREE ON. Measured over every published column: id, label, tier, role and derived never disagree between two schedules naming the same mark, and parent, constraint_tier, rationale and source_note do -- parent 156 times. A node's IDENTITY is shared; its place in a hierarchy and its annotations belong to the schedule that draws it, and live there.

role.description: What this node is for, so a client never has to parse its id. THE DECLARED SET AND NOT THE OBSERVED ONE: internal/project declares these constants and pkg/cmd/export re-spells five of them in its step declarations, so this enum is the one list all three are held to. A role present in no published column today is still valid -- writing the enum from the corpus is the mistake docs/schema-contracts.md records about `basis` and `units`.

tiers.description: The reader's left-to-right, and which nodes stand in each. A tier the column draws no node at is absent rather than empty.

items.description: An index into the nodes table.

fund_groups.description: The fund groups this column draws, in the order the page lays the fund column out. AN ORDERED LIST AND NOT A CLOSED SET: which groups exist is the document's, the order is the packager's, and neither is enumerated here. data/funds.yaml grows a fund type without asking this file, so a schema naming the ids it expects would refuse a correct column the first time the registry grew. site/app.js held both as six-element literals that could not see a seventh; this is what replaced them.

id.description: The fund-group node's id, as it appears in the nodes table.

slug.description: The fund type, which site/style.css binds a hue to. Shipped rather than cut out of the id by the client, for the reason `role` exists: a client that parses an id is a second implementation of a vocabulary this side owns.

schedules.description: ONE ENTRY PER PRINTED SCHEDULE, AND THEY ARE NOT MERGED. Each is a different published schedule with its own provenance; folding their links into one graph would silently reconcile the cells this project keeps visibly unreconciled.

from.description: An index into the nodes table.

to.description: An index into the nodes table.

value_cents.description: Integer cents, as the document printed it. A contra row arrives already negative.

fact_ids.description: The facts this figure IS. Empty only on a derived link, which cites nothing because no page prints it.

partition.description: The ribbon divides one printed table along a second axis rather than following money the schedule prints as moving that way.

contra.description: The schedule this link is printed as a reduction of, in the words the page shows beside it. Present only on a link the document prints negative.

allOf.description: A published link cites at least one fact and names where it was read; a derived one cites nothing.

A NEGATIVE FIGURE NAMES THE SCHEDULE IT REDUCES, AND ONLY A NEGATIVE ONE DOES. The sign is what the page printed; the sentence is what a reader is owed beside a ribbon the chart draws at its magnitude. Stated as a biconditional rather than in a hand-written key check, so neither half can hold without the other.

nodes.description: The nodes this schedule draws, and its own view of them. A schedule states a parent where its hierarchy has one; the same mark may hang elsewhere, or nowhere, in another schedule of the same column.

node.description: An index into the column's node table.

allOf.description: A derived node says why it exists and what it was read from. fisc verify refuses one without both; so does this, where the schedule that draws it states them.

scopes.description: The fact-store scopes this schedule draws. AN ARRAY BECAUSE ONE OF THEM GENUINELY SPANS TWO: fund-flows joins revenue-by-fund and expenditure-by-department into one graph. The per-projection documents spell this two ways -- `scope` on four of them and `scopes` on the fifth -- and the column normalises it to the shape that can express both.
